sermon.title: Learning and Following What the Bible Says
sermon.speaker: Speaker at Vine Cluster Church (name not given in the recording)
sermon.summary: In this message a speaker at Vine Cluster Church says a worn-out Bible belongs to someone who reads it, and uses the raising of Lazarus in John 11 to show that Jesus has something else in mind when things look hopeless. He then calls hearers to put Jesus’ words into practice, using the wise man on the rock, Israel’s disobedience, the cost of discipleship and James 1:22.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added by hand, and obvious caption errors were corrected; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. The recording does not give the speaker’s name, and it is not stated whether he is Pastor Kincer or a guest. Editor notes: he reads Scripture from a modern translation, so the NKJV wording shown below differs from what he reads; at about 0:13 the captions give “belongs to someone who is” where the quote he is giving ends “someone who isn’t,” shown as [unclear]; he says “be quick to listen and slow to speak” is his favorite “proverb,” but those words are James 1:19; he says “Matthew 7:21” where the passage about the wise and foolish builders he reads is Matthew 7:24–27; the captions have “her head” in John 11:2 where the Scripture says “her hair”; several names (a spy named with Joshua, the places and the last people group in Judges 2:9 and Deuteronomy 7:1) were garbled in the captions and are marked [unclear], and “Asherah poles,” “Baals” and “intermarry” are caption corrections. He also tells of visiting a fortune teller before he came to God, and gives opinions about America, other roads to heaven and the internet; these are his own views.

faqs.question: What does he call his favorite proverb?
faqs.answer: He says it is “be quick to listen and slow to speak,” and admits “I don’t always have the ability to follow that.” He says people sometimes “jump right in” before others finish.

scriptures.text_nkjv: So then, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath;

faqs.question: What does he say about learning the hard way?
faqs.answer: He says some are stubborn, and he “had to learn the hard way,” but “when you do you never forget it.”

faqs.question: Why did everyone believe Jesus could have healed Lazarus?
faqs.answer: He says Jesus had “already made a name for himself by opening deaf ears, opening blind eyes, making the lame walk,” so “these people knew that Jesus could do these things,” but “there’s something about death being final.”

faqs.question: What point does he make about the four days in the tomb?
faqs.answer: He says after four days “decomposition starts,” so Jesus “got to put him back together.” He says Jesus then called in a loud voice “Lazarus come out,” and “the dead man came out.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: Then Jesus, again groaning in Himself, came to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone lay against it. Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to Him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.” Jesus said to her, “Did I not say to you that if you would believe you would see the glory of God?” Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. And Jesus lifted up His eyes and said, “Father, I thank You that You have heard Me. And I know that You always hear Me, but because of the people who are standing by I said this, that they may believe that You sent Me.” Now when He had said these things, He cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come forth!” And he who had died came out bound hand and foot with graveclothes, and his face was wrapped with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Loose him, and let him go.”

faqs.question: What does he say the raising of Lazarus proves?
faqs.answer: He says “even death couldn’t lay hold of a person,” and that “he proved it by raising people from the dead.”

faqs.question: Does he say a soft answer always works?
faqs.answer: He says “a soft answer turns away wrath” is not always true, but “as a general rule it does,” so “if we can apply this word to our lives we’ll see how it does work.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: A soft answer turns away wrath, But a harsh word stirs up anger.

faqs.question: What does he say about God choosing one nation, Abraham’s offspring?
faqs.answer: He says God “chose one man named Abraham” and dealt with his offspring so they could be “a light to all those around them,” but “they failed to do what God wanted them to do.”

faqs.question: Why does he say God drove out the people living in the land?
faqs.answer: He says “God drove them out because of their wickedness,” and that Israel was told “if you guys do the same thing… I’m going to drive you out.” He says “it’s two things really, it’s knowing his word and applying it to your life.”

faqs.question: What does he say about people who think all roads lead to heaven?
faqs.answer: He says people who don’t read their Bible or go to a church that preaches Scripture “going to be believing every stupid thing that comes along,” such as “there really are more roads to heaven than just one,” and he says “no they don’t.”

faqs.question: What does he say carrying your cross means?
faqs.answer: He says in Rome those crucified “had to carry it to their own death,” so “carrying your own cross is a way of saying that you’re willing to lay your life down for him if necessary.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he cannot be My disciple. And whoever does not bear his cross and come after Me cannot be My disciple.

faqs.question: Why does he say the twelve stayed when the crowd left?
faqs.answer: He says when Jesus preached a hard message the twelve said “where are we going to go,” because “they knew him,” while the others “were just there because they wanted fish and bread.”

scriptures.text_nkjv: From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more. Then Jesus said to the twelve, “Do you also want to go away?” But Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”

faqs.question: What does he say about following Paul’s example?
faqs.answer: He says Paul said “imitate or follow me as I follow Christ,” so “it’s okay to follow them as long as they’re going in the right direction,” but “if they don’t follow Christ you don’t follow them.”
